breakdown.description: The prompt sets the free-end rotation to zero, even though a cantilever’s free end is generally free to rotate under an end point load.
breakdown.reason: The ground truth fixed this inconsistency by completely removing the incorrect instruction to set the free-end rotation to zero. The agent, however, repeated the incorrect instruction: "Assume the slope at the free end is zero (θ(L) = 0) as specified..." This fails to resolve the issue as the ground truth did.

breakdown.description: The prompt treats the bending moment as constant and equal to P L over the entire span, even though the cantilever moment varies linearly from the free end to the fixed end.
breakdown.reason: The ground truth resolved this inconsistency by removing the incorrect instruction to use a constant moment. The agent did the opposite and explicitly included the user's incorrect instruction in the generated specification: "For the deflection calculation, assume the bending moment is constant at M = P × L ... over the full span".
